About

Product designer and design educator in Mumbai.

Sania Shaikh
Assistant Professor, Product Design & Postgraduate Design
ISDI Parsons | Atlas SkillTech University

I work on how generative AI changes the way design is taught, and I build the courses, projects and patents that put it into practice.

I have taught at ISDI Parsons, Atlas SkillTech University since May 2023, after training industrial designers in Fusion 360 and Alias for Rubika, France. Before that I led furniture and product design at an interior design studio in Pune. That mix of studio and classroom shapes how I teach: design reasoning first, tools second, and every project tested against manufacture and market.

My courses cover product, furniture, immersive and game design, 3D modelling and rendering, digitalised industrial design, 3D printing, emerging technologies and strategic design. Students use Adobe Creative Cloud, Rhinoceros, Fusion 360, Maya, 3ds Max and Unity, and learn to frame Business Model Canvas thinking around their concepts.

Next, I want to take this into doctoral research on AI-augmented design education, adaptive learning and human-centred educational technology.

          Digital twins of places in Mumbai.

          Interactive models built for teaching digital transformation. Each one separates public context, simulated data and anything that would need field data.

          01

          CSMT

          Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus · Station digital twin

          An interactive 3D digital twin of Mumbai's historic terminus, built as a teaching model for digital transformation.

          open twin ↗
          02

          Mokai

          Café · Bandra, Mumbai

          A conceptual, parametric twin of a café, with day, night and rain views, six analysis views, five before-and-after scenarios, saved viewpoints and a presentation mode.

          open twin ↗
          03

          VegNonVeg

          Sneaker and streetwear retail · Mumbai

          A retail twin built from reference photographs of the store, for exploring layout and merchandising scenarios before changes are made on the shop floor.

          open twin ↗

          These are conceptual models for teaching. They use public context and simulated data, not live operations.

          Research experience

          MA Visual Effects Production

          Photorealistic 3D integration of a Range Rover Evoque into live-action footage

          Master's dissertation project

          • Investigated how a photorealistic 3D vehicle can be matched to live footage through modelling, camera tracking, HDRI lighting, rendering and compositing.
          • Practice-based method: reference and blueprint collection, detailed modelling of exterior, interior and wheels, UV mapping, shading and texturing.
          • Captured footage at Somerset House, London, with a DJI Osmo Pro and a Ricoh Theta 360 for HDRI lighting data.
          • Tracked and lens-solved in 3DEqualizer, repeating the solve until pixel deviation was low, before final render, composite and colour grade.
          • Tools: Autodesk Maya, Alias, Arnold, Nuke, 3DEqualizer, Adobe Photoshop.
